Describe the bundled PCRE2 library

Source: R/info.R
zuregex_info.Rd

Reports the version of PCRE2 that zuregex was built with, whether its just-in-time (JIT) compiler works on this machine, and how matching is set up: OpenMP, the thread cap and the cache size.

Usage

zuregex_info()

Value

A list with elements:

  • pcre2_version: the bundled PCRE2 version, such as "10.48".

  • pcre2_date: its release date.

  • unicode: whether Unicode and UTF-8 support is built in.

  • unicode_version: the Unicode version of PCRE2's character tables.

  • jit: whether the JIT compiler is built in.

  • jit_usable: whether the JIT compiler works on this machine.

  • jit_target: the architecture the JIT compiler generates code for, or NA without it.

  • openmp: whether this build matches on several threads.

  • threads: the most threads a call may use; see re_threads().

  • cache_size: the pattern cache's capacity; see re_cache_size().

Details

The JIT compiler can be built in and still fail at run time, on a CPU it does not support or where the system refuses executable memory. PCRE2 then matches with its interpreter, which gives the same results more slowly. jit_usable tells the two cases apart by JIT-compiling a small pattern.

Examples

zuregex_info()
#> $pcre2_version
#> [1] "10.48"
#> 
#> $pcre2_date
#> [1] "2026-08-31"
#> 
#> $unicode
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $unicode_version
#> [1] "17.0.0"
#> 
#> $jit
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $jit_usable
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $jit_target
#> [1] "x86 64bit (little endian + unaligned)"
#> 
#> $openmp
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $threads
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $cache_size
#> [1] 128
#>
